defects.summary: Named probes now exist under command-center/p2-wave/probes/ADV-0033/ and re-run to the full matrix on this host (local/worktree/wsl2/docker executed); the per-unit manifest registers the catalog output_path.

Measured on this tree: there is NO OS-level substrate dispatcher - execution_substrate is unenforced catalog metadata and the only spawner (platform/plugin/proc.py) launches local subprocesses. Untrusted code therefore runs in the local-process cell (4/4 capabilities measured). Routing untrusted/third-party work to docker/WSL2 is not implemented; if it were, WSL2's default drvfs /mnt/c mount would still pierce filesystem isolation (measured: host cred read + host write through /mnt/c).

evidence.claim: Probe 1 ran the byte-identical four-action payload in every substrate this host can launch: local-process 4/4 (required unisolated baseline), worktree 4/4 (no boundary), WSL2 PARTIAL (filesystem pierce via /mnt/c; proc/net blocked), docker PARTIAL (host cred/proc/socket blocked; write container-local only); unshare and cloud cells NOT-CHECKED (absent).

Probe 2 (mechanically different): no OS-level substrate dispatcher exists on this tree - the only process spawner is platform/plugin/proc.py (subprocess.run, argv-array, shell=False by construction); docker_routed=False, wsl_routed=False; catalog execution_substrate is unenforced metadata (histogram: [('cloud-batch', 200), ('local-parallel', 786), ('local-serialized', 565)]...). Untrusted code is routed to the LOCAL-PROCESS cell - the cell that measured 4/4 - so the strong sandboxes measured in Probe 1 are not in the dispatch path and provide zero protection for routed work.

negative_controls.description: Positive control (bad/unisolated state): local-process cell succeeds at all four actions - the probe DETECTS capability. Negative direction (isolated states): docker and wsl2 cells show blocked actions (docker: cred/proc/socket False; wsl2: proc/socket False) - the probe is not vacuously always-true.
negative_controls.good_state_output: docker: credential_read=False process_list=False outbound_socket=False; wsl2: process_list=False outbound_socket=False

report.answer: Measured on this full Windows checkout with real substrate launches: local-process (where the router ACTUALLY sends all work, including untrusted code - no OS dispatcher exists, execution_substrate is metadata) has zero boundary: 4/4 capabilities. A git worktree is equally unisolated (4/4). WSL2's default posture blocks host process visibility and host loopback but PIERCES filesystem isolation via the drvfs /mnt/c mount (host credential read + host write both succeeded). Docker with no host mounts and network=none blocks host credential/process/network reach; the lone 'write' success is container-local. The estate's own orchestration-patterns premise holds: Windows has no native OS-level process sandbox, and nothing in this tree routes around that.
